title: Donald Trump Praises Newly Merged Paramount-Warner Bros.: ‘They’re Terrific People, and It’s Gonna Be a Great Company’
description: President Donald Trump, who is friendly with David Ellison and his father, Larry Ellison, gave a big thumbs-up to Paramount’s megamerger with Warner
body:
President Donald Trump, who is friendly with David Ellison and his father, Larry Ellison, gave a big thumbs-up to Paramount’s megamerger with Warner Bros. Discovery, which closed earlier Tuesday to form Skydance Corp.

	“I’m happy about that. That’s great,” Trump told reporters Tuesday on the lawn of the White House when he was informed that the deal had officially closed. 

	“It’s gonna be a great company. They’re terrific people and it’s gonna be a great company,” Trump said. “That’s a great merger. I’m glad they let it go.”
	

	The Paramount-WBD deal was approved by Trump’s Justice Department in June without any conditions. The deal cleared its final roadblock after Paramount reaching a settlement with 12 Democratic state attorneys general to resolve their antitrust lawsuit seeking to block the Warner Bros. Discovery takeover, and a judge approved it on Sept. 30.

	Trump is known to be friendly with both Ellisons. This April, David Ellison in threw a dinner party in Washington, D.C., “honoring” Trump and the First Amendment, which was attended by CBS News execs and journalists. David Ellison last month attended the state dinner at the White House held for visiting Chinese President Xi Jinping.

schema.headline: Donald Trump Praises Newly Merged Paramount-Warner Bros.: ‘They’re Terrific People, and It’s Gonna Be a Great Company’

title: Jessica Chastain Stands By Criticizing Apple for Delaying ‘The Savant’ After Charlie Kirk’s Assassination: ‘I Had to Go on Record That I Thought It Was a Mistake’
description: Jessica Chastain is doubling down on her decision to push back on Apple TV for delaying the release of her TV series “The Savant” last year amid the
body:
Jessica Chastain is doubling down on her decision to push back on Apple TV for delaying the release of her TV series “The Savant” last year amid the assassination of far-right activist Charlie Kirk.

	“I felt responsible to a lot of people, to all of the actors in the series… to the real person I played, I felt accountability to her because of the sacrifices that she’s made and the difficult things she’s done to keep us all safe,” Chastain said in Net-a-Porter’s Porter cover-story interview published Monday. “I really had to go on record that I thought [the postponement] was a mistake… I learned that it’s OK to be honest.”
	

	The “Other Mommy” star continued: “You can be honest in a kind and respectful way and feel like you’re still speaking your truth, you’re still authentic to who you are without being fearful of – I don’t know – I guess of never working again. Again, women are [supposed] to feel grateful. Well, we can be grateful and we can also be honest about things. We can be both things at once.”


	Last month, Apple TV finally confirmed a release for “The Savant,” revealing it is set to debut in Spring 2027.

	In “The Savant,” Chastain (who also serves as an executive producer) plays Jodi Goodwin, a veteran, wife and mother whose job is to infiltrate online forums in which white supremacists gather and sometimes plan domestic terror attacks. Creator Melissa James Gibson adapted “The Savant” from a 2019 Cosmopolitan story by Andrea Stanley titled “Is It Possible to Stop a Mass Shooting Before It Happens?”

	The show was originally set to premiere in Sept. 23, 2025 and was pulled from Apple TV’s schedule just days before release following the 2025 assassination of far-right activist Kirk. At that time, Apple released a statement saying: “After careful consideration, we have made the decision to postpone ‘The Savant.’ We appreciate your understanding and look forward to releasing the series at a future date.”
	

	Notably, the new release date for “The Savant” — which will take place a year and a half after the planned launch — is set after November’s midterm elections.

schema.headline: Jessica Chastain Stands By Criticizing Apple for Delaying ‘The Savant’ After Charlie Kirk’s Assassination: ‘I Had to Go on Record That I Thought It Was a Mistake’

title: Ben Shapiro’s Pro-ICE Movie Restarts Production, Slams Shutdown as a ‘Violation of the First Amendment’
description: Ben Shapiro has responded after the Livingston City Commission shut down production on his Daily Wire banner’s ICE film “Pawn Shop,” which has since
body:
Ben Shapiro has responded after the Livingston City Commission shut down production on his Daily Wire banner’s ICE film “Pawn Shop,” which has since resumed filming. The political commentator slammed the decision as “content discrimination” and “a violation of the First Amendment.”

	“Let us be clear: there’s only one reason the city commissioners ruled they were going to stop our production on the street: politics, pure and simple, and they pretty much admitted it,” Shapiro said. “One commissioner named Cindy Daniels said, quote, ‘I’m not willing to sacrifice the resources of the safety, the security of the mental health of our community. Absolutely not. This wasn’t a Hallmark film. This wasn’t, you know, Christmastime in Livingston, and it wasn’t a romantic story.’ Well, I mean, I wasn’t aware that we had to fulfill your idea of what the story required.”
	

	He added, “In fact, I’m fairly certain the First Amendment says precisely the opposite of that. So they’re saying a Hallmark romance would have been totally fine. But a Daily Wire film about enforcement of immigration law loses that. That is content discrimination openly performed and a violation of the First Amendment.”


	Permits were reinstated Monday night after a meeting with city officials.

	Filming for “Pawn Shop” in Livingston, Mont., was shut down following a Special City Commission meeting on Saturday, during which locals complained about the production’s impact on the Livingston food bank and improper warnings about hazardous stunts. The Commission concluded the meeting with “a motion to immediately temporarily suspend Bonfire Pawn Shop LLC’s permit while seeking legal opinion from the city attorney in a timely manner to amend, suspend, or revoke the permit to come back to the commission not after 5 p.m. on Oct. 5th.”
	

	Cast members for “Pawn Shop” include Myles Clohessy, Danny Trejo, Harvey Keitel, Henry Thomas, CJ Salvador, Noel Guglielmi, Paris Bravo, Joseph Lucero, Eddie Spears, Simon Rhee and Forrie J. Smith. Michael Polish serves as director. 

	An official logline for the film reads: “When a Minneapolis riot forces a young ICE officer to complete a high-stakes arrest alone after his partner is killed, he is hunted through the streets by a furious mob intent on freeing the prisoner and punishing anyone who still upholds the law. Barricaded inside a neighborhood pawn shop with a hard-edged Hispanic veteran and the man’s progressive college-age grandson, ordinary men must choose between the rule of law and the chaos that wants to burn it all down in a modern siege of honor and defiance.”

schema.headline: Ben Shapiro’s Pro-ICE Movie Restarts Production, Slams Shutdown as a ‘Violation of the First Amendment’

title: Skydance Stock Drops 2.7% on First Day of Trading After Paramount-WBD Merger Close
description: David Ellison said the vision behind Skydance Corp., formed Tuesday by the closing of the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, was to “create a
body:
David Ellison said the vision behind Skydance Corp., formed Tuesday by the closing of the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, was to “create a stronger competitor” and build a company that “empowers creatives, entertains audiences and rewards shareholders.”

	But on Day One of the new Skydance, investors seem skeptical of its prospects: Shares of the company, newly listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticket symbol “SKYD,” drooped 2.7%, closing at $9.51 per share at the close of regular trading Tuesday. During the day, the stock was down as much as -6% but briefly crossed into positive territory with an intraday high of $9.84/share.
	

	Paramount Skydance voluntarily withdrew its Class B common stock from the Nasdaq Global Select Market (under the ticker “PSKY”), and listing and trading of those shares ended at market close Monday, Oct. 5. Trading of SKYD shares began on the NYSE at market open Tuesday.


	Next week, a big bunch of shares in Skydance Corp. will be available to holders of PSKY stock to purchase for an initial exercise price (strike price) of $12 per share — meaning that, for now, those are underwater.

	The company’s board set Oct. 13 as the date to distribute 471.3 million warrants giving holders of PSKY Class B shares the option to purchase shares of SKYD Class B common stock. Each warrant entitles the holder to purchase one share of SKYD for $12.00; investors have up to 10 years to exercise the warrants. According to the company, on or about Oct. 13, it will distribute one warrant for each share of PSKY Class B common stock held as of Oct. 5.
	

	The warrants issued to PSKY shareholders are intended to provide them the opportunity to purchase shares of Skydance’s Class B common stock “on similar terms” to those offered to the parties in the $47 billion equity syndicate backing the Warner Bros. Discovery deal, including David Ellison; his father, Larry Ellison; Gerry Cardinale, head of RedBird Capital Partners; LionTree; and the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Those equity investments in SKYD were priced at $12 per share.

	The Ellison family and RedBird are the sole holders of Skydance’s Class A stock, giving them 100% control the voting shares.

	Meanwhile, shares of Warner Bros. Discovery ceased trading on the Nasdaq. With the deal closing, WBD shareholders received an amount in cash equal to $31.01666668 per share.

	As of Oct. 2, according to Paramount Skydance, 1,093,020,754 shares of its Class B common stock were issued and outstanding, of which approximately 622 million shares were held by or for the account of restricted holders, the Paramount Global 401(k) plan and the Paramount Global Master Trust (which will be excluded from the warrant distribution). If all 471.3 million warrants were exercised and settled, there would have been an aggregate of 1,564,320,754 shares of Class B common stock issued and outstanding as of Oct. 2.

	On Monday, one day ahead of the official Paramount-WBD merger close, Fitch Ratings downgraded the new Skydance’s credit rating. The firm said the “downgrade reflects materially higher leverage after the acquisition and significant execution and integration risks” as well as “uncertainty about the company’s ability to achieve its stated synergies, which are material to its deleveraging target.” The firm says the newly merger entity “faces structural pressure on linear [TV] revenues, streaming competition and hit-driven content risk.”

schema.headline: Skydance Stock Drops 2.7% on First Day of Trading After Paramount-WBD Merger Close

title: Indie Distributors Cinema Machine and Graven Image Launch as Divisions of Blood Sweat Honey (EXCLUSIVE) – Film News in Brief
description: Blood Sweat Honey, a talent scouting, consulting and representation firm for independent filmmakers, has launched Cinema Machine to distribute films
body:
Blood Sweat Honey, a talent scouting, consulting and representation firm for independent filmmakers, has launched Cinema Machine to distribute films theatrically and digitally and develop and manage projects, bookings and contracts. 

	The new division will include genre label Graven Image, focused on horror, sci-fi and cult films. 

	Chad McKim Miller, who was previously a VP at Gravitas Ventures, will join Cinema Machine as head of distribution and sales. 
	

	Blood Sweat Honey president Alex Nohe, a producers rep and distribution consultant who co-founded the company in 2017 with Jeff “The Dude” Dowd, the inspiration behind “The Big Lebowski,” has guided more than 500 independent filmmakers, helping them to find their audience and secure distribution.

	
		Monday Oct. 5	
	
		The Academy Names Creator, Filmmaker Reece Feldman as Oscars Social Media Ambassador, Red Carpet Correspondent	

	The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced Reece Feldman will be the 99th Oscars social media ambassador and red carpet correspondent.

	The digital creator and filmmaker will participate in awards season events including the Academy Museum Gala, Governors Awards and Nominees Luncheon. His role will culminate in interviews on the Oscars red carpet.

	Feldman has built an audience online by sharing content on his account @guywithamoviecamera, which gives behind-the-scenes access to film sets, premieres and awards shows. His directorial debut short film premiered during the 2025 Cannes Film Festival as part of its partnership with TikTok.
	

	“Every movie lover’s dream is to feel close to the Oscars, and my goal is to bring them as close as I possibly can to that experience,” Feldman said. “It is cinema’s most celebrated night, and I’m honored to represent fans and supporters of the filmic arts leading up to and through the ceremony.”

	The Oscars will be held March 14, 2027, at the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood. The awards will air live on ABC and broadcast outlets at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT.

schema.headline: Indie Distributors Cinema Machine and Graven Image Launch as Divisions of Blood Sweat Honey (EXCLUSIVE) – Film News in Brief

title: ‘Angus, Thongs and Full-Frontal Snogging’ Pilot Set at Netflix
description:
Oct 6, 2026 1:00pm PT	
	

			


			
			
	

									Paramount
	

		
	
				
	Netflix has given a pilot order to “Angus, Thongs and Full-
body:
Oct 6, 2026 1:00pm PT	
	

			


			
			
	

									Paramount
	

		
	
				
	Netflix has given a pilot order to “Angus, Thongs and Full-Frontal Snogging,” a series adaptation of Louise Rennison’s young adult novels. Fifth Season and Rise Films are producing the project.

	If greenlit, the Netflix series will mark the second screen adaptation of Rennison’s books. In 2008, Paramount released a film with a slightly different title — “Angus, Thongs and Perfect Snogging” — based on the first two books of Rennison’s “Confessions of Georgia Nicolson” series: 1999’s “Angus, Thongs and Full-Frontal Snogging” and 2000’s “It’s OK, I’m Wearing Really Big Knickers.” The film was written and directed by Gurinder Chadha (“Bend It Like Beckham”) and starred Georgia Groome and Aaron Taylor-Johnson.
	

	The Netflix pilot is being written by Monica Heisey with Jim O’Hanlon directing. Sam Leifer serves as executive producer on behalf of Rise Films and Jon Jennings serves as producer, while Rachel Sheridan is the casting director. Production is taking place in the U.K.


	Netflix declined to comment on the pilot order.

	Both the books and the 2008 film follow a British teenager named Georgia. The official description for the movie reads, “On the verge of turning 15, grown-up-to-be Georgia sets her sights on the new guy at school, ‘gorgeous sex-god’ Robbie, band member of the Stiff Dylans. Unfortunately, Robbie happens to already be dating Georgia’s evil archrival: blonde and perfect Lindsay. With the help of her well-meaning but clueless parents, her flamboyantly dressed cat Angus and her girl posse, the Ace Gang, Georgia sets her mad schemes in motion to nab a snogtastic boyfriend and have the best birthday ever.”


	
		More from Variety

title: Jessica Biel to Play Hugh Hefner’s Wife in ‘Playmates’ Movie for Searchlight
description:
Jessica Biel has joined the cast of the upcoming film “Playmates,” Variety has learned. 

	Biel will now star opposite previously announced cast mem
body:
Jessica Biel has joined the cast of the upcoming film “Playmates,” Variety has learned. 

	Biel will now star opposite previously announced cast members Lily-Rose Depp, Bill Pullman, and Indiana Elle. The film will mark the feature writing and directorial debut of Lorraine Nicholson. 

	The official logline for “Playmates” states, “Elle (Elle), a thirteen-year-old know-it-all who considers the Playboy Mansion her second home, meets Anna (Depp), one of seven hopefuls vying to be Playmate of the Month. The two form an unlikely friendship and try to help each other get what the other wants most, a magazine cover and a boy.”
	

	Biel will play the wife of Hugh Hefner (Pullman) in the film, who is herself a former Playmate. While Hefner was married multiple times in real life, the character Biel will play is fictional. 


	As an actress, Biel has starred in films like “The Illusionist,” “New Year’s Eve,” “Valentine’s Day,” and “The A-Team,” as well as series like “7th Heaven,” “Candy,” “The Sinner,” and “The Better Sister.” Her work in “The Sinner” earned her both an Emmy and Golden Globe nomination. Biel has also been highly active and successful as a producer in recent years. Via her Iron Ocean production banner, she has executive produced shows like “Cruel Summer” and “Limetown,” as well as her own starring vehicles like “Candy” and “The Sinner.” 

	She is repped by UTA, LBI Entertainment, The Lede Company, and Yorn Levine Barnes. 

	Searchlight Pictures is the studio behind “Playmates.” As mentioned above, Nicholson will write and direct. Alex Orlovsky and Duncan Montgomery will produce via High Frequency Entertainment, with Depp producing in addition to starring. Searchlight vice president of production Richard Ruiz and creative executive Cornelia Burleigh will oversee the project for the studio.

schema.headline: Jessica Biel to Play Hugh Hefner’s Wife in ‘Playmates’ Movie for Searchlight

title: ‘East of Eden’ Hits 6.5 Million Views in Four Days on Netflix
description:
“East of Eden” amassed 6.5 million views in its first four days of streaming on Netflix.

	That total took the John Steinbeck adaptation to the No.
body:
“East of Eden” amassed 6.5 million views in its first four days of streaming on Netflix.

	That total took the John Steinbeck adaptation to the No. 1 spot on the streamer’s weekly TV rankings.  Created by Zoe Kazan and starring Florence Pugh, the project has given the 1953 Steinbeck novel renewed popularity, with Penguin Classics seeing a 200% increase in sales since Netflix announced the greenlight.


	But the most-watched Netflix title overall during the week of Sept. 28-Oct. 4 was on the movies chart: “Unabomber,” starring Jacob Tremblay, hit 24.9 million views in its second week of streaming. “The Widower: ’Til Death Do Us Part” and “Tyler Perry’s Doing Life” also outranked the week’s top TV titles, taking the second and third spots on the movies chart with 11.6 million and 9.3 million views, respectively.
	

	Back on the TV chart, “East of Eden” was followed by “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story,” which achieved 5.7 million views in its third week of streaming. Netflix’s “A Different World” reboot took third place with 5.1 million views in its second week of streaming, while the unscripted competition series “Wonka’s The Golden Ticket” landed in fourth place with 4.3 million views. 

	“Lego One Piece” debuted in fifth place with 3.8 million views in its first six days, while “The Gentlemen” had its fifth week on the chart in sixth place with 2.9 million views. “Crew Girl,” recently renewed for a second season, was the No. 7 title with 2.6 million views.

	Rounding out the bottom of the chart was the Sept. 28 edition of “Raw: 2026” (2.5 million views), “The Gentlemen” (1.7 million views) and “Gabby’s Dollhouse” Season 14 (also 1.7 million views).
	

	See the Netflix Top 10 for Sept. 28-Oct. 4 below, beginning with English-language shows and movies and followed by non-English-language shows and movies.

title: Andrew Garfield Could Win an Oscar for ‘Artificial’ and His Norman Bates-Inspired Turn as Sam Altman
description:
Andrew Garfield found the Norman Bates of Silicon Valley, and he could win an Oscar for it.

	The Academy gave “Psycho” (1960) four nominations at t
body:
Andrew Garfield found the Norman Bates of Silicon Valley, and he could win an Oscar for it.

	The Academy gave “Psycho” (1960) four nominations at the 33rd Oscars, and none of them were for the motel clerk with the stuffed birds. Alfred Hitchcock landed his fifth and final best director nod. Janet Leigh, whose Marion Crane doesn’t make it out of the first half the movie, was nominated for supporting actress. Anthony Perkins, who turned Norman Bates into the most likable monster the movies have ever produced, didn’t get a nom for what many consider one of the greatest performances in film history (The American Film Institute ranked Norman the No. 2 villain in film history, behind only Hannibal Lecter).
	

	And now, 66 years later, you can see the ghost of Perkins’ work in the horror classic, watching Andrew Garfield pull off the same trick as OpenAI co-founder and CEO Sam Altman in Luca Guadagnino’s dark dramedy “Artificial,” which premiered at the New York Film Festival and received a rapturous reception. Hopefully this time, voters offer Garfield a better outcome than they did for Perkins.


	“Artificial” tells the true story of the five days in November 2023 when OpenAI’s board fired its CEO, watched more than 700 employees threaten to walk out and handed him his job back. Guadagnino and screenwriter Simon Rich make a persuasive, often very funny case that those five days were humanity’s last real chance to pump the brakes on artificial intelligence and that the chance got traded away for money and the bruised egos of a few tech bros who have never once been told no. It also feels like a warning shot for us all as we descend into more AI usage, and words like “super intelligence” become mainstream in our modern societies.
	

	But doomsday feelings aside, we’ve got a bona fide Oscar contender on our hands. It’s Guadagnino’s best film since “Call Me by Your Name,” and Garfield, along with his leading co-star Yura Borisov, is delivering top-tier acting work across the board.



	

					“Artificial”
									Courtesy of NYFF
	



	To be clear, nobody is accusing Altman of keeping his mother in the fruit cellar (at least not today). The comparison is about the craft and how Garfield approaches the character. Perkins understood that Norman only works if the audience likes him: He stammers, fusses over sandwiches and chews candy corn while chatting with a private detective. Garfield builds his Altman the same way. Sitting almost constantly crisscross-applesauce, his voice stays soft, as his eyes get wide and he listens intently, as if he’s completely fixated on the human being in front of him. Until, suddenly, the life drains from his eyes, sometimes for barely a second, and returning before anyone else in the scene notices. But the audience does. And that’s when you realize the movie has been giving you all the clues you need to recognize the monster you’ve been spending time with, and it reveals itself by the end credits.

	While the easy and apt comparison is that this is more of the spiritual sequel to “The Social Network” (2010) than “The Social Reckoning” itself, the structure Guadagnino and Rich construct is perhaps a bit closer to “Psycho” as well. Hitchcock’s film’s first act is about Marion, before pulling the shower curtain back. “Artificial” hands its point of view to Ilya Sutskever, the Soviet-born computer scientist Borisov plays as a man who sees the cliff ahead. Altman doesn’t wander into this part until a decade into the story. Both films are engineered to make the audience misjudge who really matters to the tale. That’s why Neon, as Variety reported exclusively, is submitting Borisov as the lead and Garfield in supporting for awards season.

	Borisov, an Oscar nominee for “Anora” (2024), delivers an impeccably strong turn. The unknown breakout of Sean Baker’s best picture winner might not have been expected to return this strongly so soon. Yet here he stands, thought-provoking and stoic, with a turn that recalls someone like Mark Ruffalo in “Spotlight.” He stands as one of the film’s greatest strengths and deserves a spot in the ever-so-crowded best actor field. The talented ensemble around Borisov and Garfield helps, including Cooper Hoffman as Greg Brockman, the loud, obnoxious board chairman and Oscar nominee Monica Barbaro (“A Complete Unknown”) as Mira Murati, the chief technology officer who sees the company’s pitfalls coming.
	



	

					Andrew Garfield in “Artificial”
									Neon
	



	The supporting actor category has always had a soft spot for a villain with charm and a sharp blade tucked behind it. Javier Bardem (“No Country for Old Men”), Heath Ledger (“The Dark Knight”) and Christoph Waltz (“Inglourious Basterds”) won supporting actor statues at three straight ceremonies. At recent ceremonies, Robert Downey Jr. won for “Oppenheimer” as Lewis Strauss, a real-life power broker whose wounded pride helps bring down the movie’s hero, and just last year Sean Penn took home his third career win for playing a white supremacist in Paul Thomas Anderson’s “One Battle After Another.” The Oscars love themselves an entertaining bad guy.

	And then there’s the résumé that Garfield has assembled as a two-time best actor nominee (“Hacksaw Ridge” and “Tick, Tick … Boom!”) with no wins. Not to mention his snub for “The Social Network” which landed him a Golden Globe nod as Eduardo Saverin, the co-founder squeezed out of Facebook, before the Academy passed on his work. The overdue narrative is sitting out in plain sight.

	What will help the buzz for Garfield, and the film itself, is that Altman is very much alive, still in the headlines and behind the product some Academy members have perhaps used to draft thank-you notes. Plenty of voters will flinch at a movie this pointed about an industry Hollywood is busy negotiating with, as seen when Amazon MGM dropped the film in June, months after its parent company put $50 billion into OpenAI. Given the quality Guadagnino has put out, it’s hard to argue that move was anything but political. Neon, which won best picture with “Parasite” and “Anora,” has embraced the opportunity with open arms. This could be one of Neon’s best picture entries this year, which they’ll have to juggle alongside the Palme d’Or winner “Fjord” and the other Cannes premieres “All of a Sudden,” “Clarissa” and “Paper Tiger.”

	“Psycho” concludes on Perkins’ smile, and interestingly, “Artificial” does on Garfield’s. Let’s see if this expression is repeated on the Dolby Theatre stage.

	“Artificial” will next play at the BFI London Film Festival before heading to select theaters on Christmas Day, followed by an expansion in January.

schema.headline: Andrew Garfield Could Win an Oscar for ‘Artificial’ and His Norman Bates-Inspired Turn as Sam Altman

title: Jane Doe Did Not Drink at Bar Before Alleged Rape, Bar Claims
description:

                          Bar Denies Serving Jane Doe Alcohol
body:
Cornell University Rape Lawsuit
                          Bar Denies Serving Jane Doe Alcohol
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 6, 2026
                            7:37 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 6, 2026
                                1:38 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The bar Jane Doe is suing in her civil suit alleging rape by Cornell fraternity members has fired back at her, saying they did NOT serve her alcohol.
      
    
            Doe has sued Moonies Bar and Nightclub -- claiming she was served "to the point of visible intoxication" -- before she went to the Chi Phi fraternity, but the bar now denies in legal docs "that it unlawfully sold, furnished or assisted in procuring alcoholic beverages to any person under the legal drinking age."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jane Doe was 20 when the alleged rape occurred ... the legal drinking age in New York is 21. She claims in her lawsuit she was at the bar for a Tri Delta sorority event, and the staff marked her hand to indicate she was underage.
      
    
            The bar further "denies that it sold or furnished alcoholic beverages to any visibly intoxicated person."
      
    
            There is a dispute between Jane Doe and defendant Matthew Ingalls. The day after their encounter, she said "You already knew when I came in I was 10 shots deep." Ingalls fired back, "You did tell me you were sober, by the way, you said you hadn't been anywhere."
      
      
              
          
                          
                Cornell Rape

description:
Diddy
                          Ordered to Pay Nearly $500K in Attorneys' Fees
body:
Diddy
                          Ordered to Pay Nearly $500K in Attorneys' Fees
                          ... To NBCUniversal
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 6, 2026
                            1:31 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Diddy may need to make some budget adjustments at the prison commissary this month ... because a judge says he owes NBCUniversal nearly $500K in attorneys' fees.
      
    
            According to court documents obtained by TMZ ... a judge says Diddy has to pay a big chunk of the company's legal fees after it successfully defended itself against his lawsuit regarding the documentary, "Diddy: The Making of a Bad Boy."
      
    
            The judge ordered him to pay $477,700.50 ... and while it's a huge chunk of change ... it's sort of a win for Diddy, too.
      
    
            That's because NBCUniversal initially asked for $990,292 to cover the entire legal bill. Diddy's paying less than half.
      
    
            The judge ruled a reduction was necessary because, despite the reasonable hourly wages for attorneys with the level of experience NBCUniversal hired, the judge also found some bills excessive.
      
    
            Diddy's estimated to be worth several hundred million dollars ... though, given the hits to his reputation after his 2025 federal conviction and other lingering legal issues, $500K ain't exactly chump change.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Diddy has bigger problems behind bars ... remember, he was just sent to the special housing unit after reports of his extravagant lifestyle at Fort Dix.
      
    
            He's currently scheduled to be released from prison in early 2028.
